correctness.rationale: For exactly three occupied indices, an admissible sign assignment exists iff a same-sign pair passes two explicit reflection checks. The three pair tests give an exhaustive dichotomy: an outer-pair domain plus two disjoint reflected arithmetic-progression exceptions. Their counts are exact finite arithmetic sums for every \(n\ge3\), not fitted from data. Six algebraic residue evaluations give the leading coefficient \(11/108\), and the exceptions are quadratic, hence the ratio \(11/18\). The packaged direct signing checker covers every support through \(n=41\) and checks the symbolic forms through \(n=1000\).

value.rationale: Three nonzero slots are the first phase-assignment layer in which a constraint failure is possible: one or two slots can always be given pairwise different signs. The exact classification and the constant \(11/18\) quantify the sparse optical-codeword supply. Without phase choices the same fixed-weight layer has only \(O(n^2)\) BGP-admissible supports, versus a positive fraction of \(\binom n3\) under TGP. This isolates a natural first obstruction and determines an otherwise unreported exact first-layer invariant; no claim concerning unrestricted capacity is needed.
